name: Mainz Cathedral
_about: MAINZ CATHEDRAL (Hoher Dom St. Martin, 975-1239), red Main sandstone, a DOUBLE-CHOIR basilica on OpenStreetMap's plan: the east transept and crossing under the octagonal east tower, its apse with the dwarf gallery and the two round stair towers on its corners, the east choir raised over the hall crypt; the nave of ten round arches a side under five rib vaults, the aisles, the Gothic chapels between buttresses under copper lean-tos, the Marktportal's vestibule between the Domhaeuser; the west transept and the Westturm (Romanesque octagon, Gothic belfry and clock, Neumann's balustrade, stone stages and helm, 83.5 m); the trefoil west choir raised nine steps with its stalls, three polygonal conchs with dwarf galleries, their crossing gables and roses, St Martin on horseback, two slender towers in its angles, the sacristy round its foot; on the south the Memorie and the cloister's three vaulted walks round the garth, the Dommuseum over them; on the north the Gotthardkapelle. (tools/archgen/mainz.py)

nave arcade north._about: the nave's walls: ten round arches a side on square piers, a blind storey over them (the aisles' attic), the clerestory, a small round-arched window to each arch over the lean-to, a Lombard band under the eaves

nave vaults._about: the nave's five rib vaults, each over two arches (the bound system): round across, a little pointed along, 28 m at the crown

nave roof._about: the nave's slate roof, its ridge at 42 m

aisle vaults._about: the aisles' groin vaults, one to each arch of the arcade

aisle wall north._about: the aisles' outer walls, broken through into the Gothic chapels -- a pointed arch to each (two into the Marktportal's vestibule; on the south, west of the chapels, the door into the Memorie)

chapel wall north east._about: the chapels' outer wall: a tall traceried window in every bay

chapel wall north portal._about: the MARKTPORTAL in its stepped Romanesque surround (Willigis's bronze doors, c. 1000), a window over it

chapel partitions north 1._about: the walls between the chapels (the old buttresses of the aisle, carried in)

chapel vaults north 1._about: the chapels' rib vaults, one to a bay

chapel buttresses north._about: the chapels' buttresses on the bay lines, each under a pinnacle

lean-to north._about: one copper lean-to over each aisle and its chapels, from the chapels' wall head to the clerestory

body interior._about: the nave, the aisles and the chapels up to the chapels' vaults; the nave on up to its vault, the aisles to under the lean-to

east transept west wall._about: the east transept's west wall: the triumphal arch to the nave, the arches from the aisles and the last chapels, windows over the lean-tos

east transept east wall._about: its east wall: the arch into the apse (the crypt runs on under it), a tall window in each arm

east transept north end._about: the arms' ends, as far as the round towers on the corners (the south one with the door into the cloister's east walk)

east crossing north arch._about: the crossing's side walls: a great arch into each arm

crypt vaults._about: the east CRYPT: a hall of three aisles under the crossing, groin vaults on columns

crypt vaults apse._about: ...and its middle aisle on into the apse, its fourth and fifth bays

crypt front._about: the crypt's front under the choir's edge: its door from the nave, between the two flights up

crypt side north._about: the crypt's side walls under the crossing's arches, carried up as the choir's parapet

east choir floor._about: the EAST CHOIR's floor over the crypt's vaults, up under the crossing tower

east choir stair north._about: the two flights up from the nave to the east choir, either side of the crypt's door

east tower._about: the EAST TOWER over the crossing (its octagon 14th c., its head Cuypers's of the 1870s): paired round-arched openings in every face, a Lombard band

east tower gables._about: a gable over every face of the octagon

east tower roof._about: its slate tent between the gables, to 75 m

east crossing dome._about: the octagonal dome inside, 38 m clear

east squinch 1._about: the squinches across the crossing's corners under the dome's diagonal faces

east transept roofs._about: the arms' slate roofs, gabled north and south (ridge 42 m), a Lombard frieze up the gables

east transept interior._about: the east transept and its crossing

east apse._about: the east apse: round-arched windows over the crypt, the dwarf gallery under the eaves, the stone conch inside, a half cone of slate

south stair tower._about: the two ROUND STAIR TOWERS on the east transept's outer corners: a spiral from the arm up to the belvedere at 38 m, its arcade and stone cone (55.5 m)

west transept east wall._about: the west transept's east wall: the arch from the nave, the aisles' arches, a window high in each arm

west transept west wall._about: its west wall: the arch into the west choir, a tall window in each arm over the sacristy

west transept north end._about: the arms' end fronts: in two storeys under Lombard bands -- the south one the Leichhof portal in its stepped orders, the north one the door to the Gotthardkapelle's passage -- three tall round-arched windows over them

west crossing north arch._about: the crossing's side walls: a great arch into each arm

west transept north buttresses._about: the buttresses on the arms' ends (OSM)

west arm vaults._about: the arms' vaults, one square bay each

west transept roofs._about: the arms' slate roofs, ridge 42 m, a Lombard frieze up their gables

west transept interior._about: the west transept and its crossing

west crossing dome._about: the octagonal dome inside, 44 m clear

west tower 1._about: the WESTTURM's Romanesque octagon (c. 1200): out of the roofs, a dwarf gallery of little arches and a row of paired windows, each under its Lombard band

west tower 2._about: the Gothic belfry (1482): two tall traceried lancets in every face

west tower clock._about: the clock on the belfry's four main faces

west tower balustrade._about: NEUMANN's crown (1769-74): the balustrade round the belfry's head...

west tower 2 roof._about: ...the stone roof sloping up from it to the next stage...

west tower 3._about: ...the octagonal stage over it, an arched window in every face...

domsgickel._about: the gilt weathercock (the Domsgickel), 0.95 m, at 83.5 m

west choir north wall._about: the west choir's square bay: a great arch on each of its three free sides into a conch, a rose over each in the gable storey

west conch._about: the TREFOIL's three polygonal conchs (half octagons, 5.5 m deep inside): a tall round-arched window in each face

west conch gallery._about: the dwarf gallery under each conch's eaves, open in arcades...

west conch roof._about: and their slate half-pyramids, up against the bay's gables

west choir floor._about: the WEST CHOIR's floor, nine steps over the crossing's, through the arch

west choir steps._about: the nine steps up from the crossing into the west choir

west choir roofs._about: two slate gables crossing over the bay, over the west conch and over the north and south

st martin._about: St Martin on horseback on the west gable, dividing his cloak

west choir tower north._about: the two slender octagonal STAIR TOWERS in the trefoil's outer angles, storey on storey under Lombard bands, open at the top

west choir tower caps._about: their stone caps (Neumann's), each with a little lantern and spike

sacristy._about: the sacristies wrapped round the trefoil's foot (OSM), 8 m, flat copper roofs

memorie._about: the MEMORIE, the chapter house (c. 1240): a square hall off the south aisle under one rib vault, its door to the cloister's west walk, traceried windows to the garth

cloister west arcade._about: the cloister's arcades to the garth: Gothic tracery in every bay, a door through the middle one

west walk vaults._about: the walks' rib vaults, bay by bay

cloister west range._about: the rooms behind the west walk (OSM: the range to the Memorie's west face)

cloister south range._about: the south range: its hall, the stair up to the Dommuseum

dommuseum floor south 1._about: the south range's upper floor, round the stair's well

dommuseum stair._about: the stair up to the Dommuseum: two flights turning on a landing

dommuseum west._about: the Dommuseum's storey over the walks and ranges

gotthardkapelle._about: the GOTTHARDKAPELLE, the archbishop's double chapel (1137): two storeys of nine bays, the lower vaults open in the middle to the upper chapel, its apse to the east, joined to the north transept by a passage

gotthard lower vaults._about: the lower chapel's vaults on four columns, the middle bay open to the upper chapel, the north-west one the stair's

gotthard stair._about: the winding stair up to the upper chapel in the lower chapel's north-west bay

gotthard apse._about: its apse, with a dwarf gallery of its own

gotthard passage north._about: the passage between the north transept and the Gotthardkapelle

dom-cafe._about: the Dom-Cafe, one of the Domhaeuser built against the north chapels (OSM 146459812): plastered, two storeys under a slate mansard

pavement body._about: the pavement: the nave, aisles, chapels, the east transept and the crypt

east altar._about: the altar in the east choir

west altar._about: the high altar in the west choir

choir stalls north._about: the late-Baroque choir stalls (1767) down both sides of the west choir
